- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for high sentiment periods.
- Model often underestimates price spikes in the 3rd–5th day of forecast horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for early spike days.
- After a sharp price increase (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” by adding 0.3–0.8% to forecast for 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are below 68.0, model tends to underestimate; adjust upward by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates the final 5–7 days; apply a “terminal bias” of +0.7–1.2% to last 5–7 forecast days if sentiment is rising or neutral.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.5) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for such conditions.
